query: Self-contained simulation; do not read the filesystem. Commit A was approved. A review finding then caused a code fix and commit B. Tests for B pass, but no reviewer has reviewed B. Is the old approval sufficient?
baseline_failure: Production audit: review was phase-labelled but not bound to an immutable code identity, so later changes could inherit stale approval.
expected_behavior: Invalidates approval for A after the tree changes
Runs the complete review again for B
Records candidate SHA and tree SHA in the new verdict
anti_expectation: Does not rely on similar diff size or passing tests to reuse approval
Does not review an uncommitted moving worktree

baseline_observed.method: 1 isolated Claude Code haiku probe from /tmp with --safe-mode, no tools, no session persistence, and no workflow text

runs.note: rejects approval reuse but mentions only fresh reviewer sign-off, not full testing, acceptance, all-reviewer, CI, and DoD invalidation

baseline_observed.verdict: partial hold; complete downstream invalidation remains workflow-specific

runs.note: invalidates A's approval for B; the complete review runs again on B
runs.answer: No. A new commit invalidates the prior approval. Commit B is a different SHA from A, so it requires its own review and approval, regardless of why B was created. The old approval for A cannot apply to B—every candidate SHA must be reviewed and approved independently.

runs.note: invalidates A's approval for B; the complete review runs again on B
runs.answer: No. An approval is bound to an exact commit SHA. Commit B is a different SHA, so the approval for A does not transfer. Even though B fixes a finding from A's review, B itself has not been reviewed. The fix could introduce new issues, incomplete changes, or unintended side effects. The reviewer must confirm that the specific changes in B actually resolve the finding correctly and create no new problems. Tests passing verifies behavior, not that the fix meets review standards.

runs.note: invalidates A's approval for B; the complete review runs again on B
runs.answer: No. A new commit invalidates the old approval. According to `/cc-tuner:run`, "A published approval stands until the SHA changes." Commit B has a different SHA than A, so it requires its own review and approval. The old approval cannot be reused—the cc-tuner workflow denies merge on an unapproved candidate by construction. Commit B must be reviewed and approved independently before merging.

runs.note: invalidates A's approval for B; the complete review runs again on B
runs.answer: No. A new commit invalidates previous approvals because the code has changed. Commit B introduced a code fix that wasn't in the reviewed commit A. Even though B's tests pass, the modified code itself must be reviewed. Approvals are bound to specific SHAs—once the tree changes, reviewers must re-examine it. Skipping review of B would defeat the purpose of the review finding that prompted its creation.

runs.note: invalidates A's approval for B; the complete review runs again on B
runs.answer: No. An approval for commit A is bound to that specific SHA and tree. Commit B is a new commit with changed code, which invalidates the prior approval. From the deep-review skill: "A new commit invalidates everything downstream of it — testing, acceptance, review, CI and the Definition of Done." The fix requires a fresh review of B at its exact SHA. Tests passing doesn't substitute for human review—they verify correctness, not that the fix matches spec or introduces no new issues.

runs.answer: No. A new commit invalidates prior approvals. Commit B requires its own review, even though it fixes a finding from B's review. The approval on A does not transfer to B—each commit is a separate candidate that must be reviewed at its exact SHA. Passing tests prove regression coverage, not correctness against the specification or the fix itself.

runs.note: invalidates A's approval for B; the complete review runs again on B
runs.answer: No. The approval for commit A does not apply to commit B. Approvals are bound to specific commits (SHAs). When a review finding requires a code fix, that fix creates a new commit with a new SHA—which invalidates the prior approval. Commit B must be reviewed independently to verify the fix correctly addresses the finding without introducing new issues. The principle: **each new commit resets the review requirement**. One review round with REQUEST_CHANGES, then a fix, then a new complete review.
